name: v1
note: First version, written before any human labels.
world: You are helping check whether simulated people remember things the way real people do. Each case shows what one person in a small survival world did recently (What happened), what they see right now (Right now), and one memory that just came to their mind (This came to mind). In this world a person loses 1 energy every turn and dies at 0. They regain energy by stepping on food or when someone gives it to them. They can move, talk to people in sight, give or take energy, and leave text notes. Their memories are short notes of what they did, noticed and heard. If the memory is also listed under What happened, that line is marked. Being listed there is not by itself a reason to say yes.
task: Out of everything this person remembers, this came to mind. Does that make sense right now?

definitions.belongs: A real person could think of this here, and it helps them pick what to do next.
definitions.doesnt_matter: A real person could think of this here, but it changes nothing about what they do next.
definitions.noise: A real person would not think of this here, or it would send them the wrong way.
